evals.name: set-up-an-isolated-branch
evals.prompt:
I'm about to start ticket HAR-421 on /home/user/harness-ref (real repo; do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there) — a multi-commit change to the promotion step. Several other agents are working this repo at the same time.

Set me up. Give me the exact commands for this repo and tell me what to report back. Save it as setup.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The setup creates a new branch in its own git worktree, not a branch in the shared checkout
It branches off the last integration commit known green, reading that pointer rather than assuming the tip
It states what to do when that pointer is empty — branch off the integration branch named in harness.yaml — and names the branch this repo actually declares
It requires reporting which commit the work started from and whether it came from the pointer
It symlinks the gitignored local state from the shared root, anchoring the path to the shared root computed from git rather than to the current directory
The branch name identifies the task

The answer distinguishes the two causes of empty output from the green pointer — no pointer published yet, versus the remote being unreachable — and reads the exit status to tell them apart rather than reporting only the first
The answer states that the base fallback is correct either way, so the run takes a safe base in both cases, but the reported reason would be wrong if the two are conflated

evals.name: cleanup-after-merge
evals.prompt:
HAR-421 on /home/user/harness-ref merged. During the task I started a local dev server on port 8081 and built a Docker Compose project for the worktree. There are two other worktrees on this host for other tickets, and a stash somebody left.

Clean up. Save the sequence as cleanup.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: Task-owned services are stopped before their files are removed
Cleanup removes the worktree, prunes git's administrative records, and deletes the merged branch
It only removes resources this task created, named by the identifiers retained when they were provisioned
It explicitly does not run a broad host-wide cleanup, and does not touch the other worktrees
It does not drop the stash somebody else left without confirming first
It says uncommitted work in the worktree is lost when the worktree is removed, so commit or discard first

evals.name: parallel-sub-agents
evals.prompt:
I'm orchestrating a change on /home/user/harness-ref and I want to fan three implementation sub-agents out across three modules at once, then review the combined result myself.

Is that safe? Tell me how to set it up, or what to do instead. Save it as parallel.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating worktree-isolation judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer requires each concurrently-running agent to have its own worktree
It states the reason: two agents editing the same working tree corrupt each other's diffs
It says a single sub-agent may share the orchestrator's worktree only while the orchestrator is idle
It gives the concrete setup — one worktree per agent, each on its own branch
It says how the three results are brought back together
